title: Actionize postmortem items into PRD: runtime guardrails, verification hooks, and rollback criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Convert recent real-traffic postmortem action items into concrete PRD requirements: introduce guardrails for model routing and cache eviction, define deterministic fallback triggers, add verification hooks (synthetic and canary), and formalize rollback criteria and runbook acceptance tests.
background: A cross-region production incident revealed three failure modes: (1) KV cache thrash under mixed-sequence traffic causing tail-latency spikes, (2) routing policy thrash when autoscale backfills created model variant oscillation, and (3) insufficient synthetic coverage for degraded serving paths. Postmortem recommended adding deterministic thresholds for fallback, clearer routing contracts, and integrated verification for rollouts. This ticket turns those action items into PRD language and acceptance tests for runtime-1.20 and console-2026.03 releases.
scope_changes: Additions: (a) new SLO gating and rollback criteria in PRD, (b) explicit fallback triggers and deterministic decision tree documented in API and runtime configs, (c) synthetic verification harness for cache/routing failure scenarios. No changes to billing model. Some UX additions to Console (deploy preview + verification status) are in scope, but full console redesign is out of scope.
requirements: 1) SLO/Alerting: Define primary signals (p99 latency, 5m error rate, kv-miss-rate) and numeric thresholds that auto-enable deterministic fallback when breached for 3 consecutive intervals. 2) Fallback decision graph: Provide a documented, runtime-enforceable decision tree that prefers cached-compatible model variants, then regional failover, then reduced-batch low-cost variant. 3) Routing stability constraint: Prevent routing churn by enforcing a 90s cooldown after autoscale or variant swap unless an emergency override is triggered. 4) Verification hooks: Canary must pass synthetic prompt set (latency + output quality) before 100% rollout; verification includes chaos-injection scenarios for KV eviction and delayed backend responses. 5) Rollback criteria: Clear SLA gates and automated rollback when verification fails or SLOs degrade beyond defined thresholds for 10m. 6) Observability: Expose the fallback decision and rationale in request traces, with a console view for recent fallback events and affected customers. 7) Runbook acceptance tests: Automatable tests that simulate the three failure modes and validate fallback path behavior and alerts.
non_goals: 1) Rewriting serving runtime internals or kernel-level optimization work (those belong to engineering epics). 2) Full redesign of the Console UX beyond adding a verification status and fallback events table. 3) Creating new paid tiers or pricing changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLO gating is specified in PRD with numerical thresholds and mapping to deterministic fallback triggers.
A2: Fallback decision tree documented and approved by runtime eng and SRE; there is a JSON/YAML schema that runtime can consume for enforcement.
A3: Canary verification harness created in CI that runs synthetic prompt set plus two chaos scenarios; green canary required for rollout to >10% traffic.
A4: Automated rollback rule in runtime triggers and executes within 2 minutes of a verified SLO breach for canary or full rollout paths.
A5: Console surfaces recent fallback events (last 72h) and links to the triggering telemetry traces and impacted API keys.
A6: Runbook tests pass in staging: simulated KV thrash, routing oscillation, and delayed backing infra; results logged and test artifacts linked.
A7: Stakeholder signoffs from SRE, runtime eng, and legal/security for any telemetry that exposes customer identifiers.
A8: Security review recorded and any data retention constraints added to PRD before release.
A9: Post-release synthetic monitors added to customer-facing SLA dashboard and baseline metrics captured for 30 days.
A10: Documentation and runbook updates published with rollout checklist and rollback playbook.
implementation_notes: - Use existing traffic-splitting and rollout flags in the runtime; add a fallback-enforcement layer that interprets the new decision graph. - Build a verification runner as a CI job that can be called by Console during canaries. - Work with Observability to add a lightweight fallback event API with minimal PII. - Engineering to estimate capacity and warm-pool sizing changes required when falling back to dedicated model variants.
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize PRD and schema (week 1). 2) Engineering implements enforcement layer and exposes fallback events (week 2-4). 3) Create canary verification harness and integrate with Console (week 3-5). 4) Staging runbook tests and cross-team signoffs (week 5). 5) Gradual rollout behind canary with automated rollback enabled (week 6-7). 6) Post-launch 30-day monitoring and retro (week 8-12).
notes: This PRD update is intentionally prescriptive: it must reduce ambiguity between runtime and SRE teams when a regression occurs. Expect follow-up smaller tickets to split the enforcement work across components. The evaluation harness should be reusable for future model onboarding flows.
